title: FEI Tribunal Decision — FEI Tribunal Final Decision Settlement Agreement Case 2025 BS07 (2025ATF02) CASTLEFIELD CORNELIOUS Ms CAMPBELL C25-0027-Corr
text:
DECISION RENDERED BY FEI TRIBUNAL
11 November 2025
in the matter of
Ms Kaitlin CAMPBELL (the “PR”) (Ref. C25-0027)
(FEI Case number: 2025/BS07 - 2025/ATF02) CASTLEFIELD CORNELIOUS
COMPOSITION OF THE FEI TRIBUNAL PANEL:
Mr Agustin Fattal Jaef, (ARG), Sole Panel Member
Ref. no. FEI Tribunal: C25-0027 CAMPBELL (2025/BS07(2025/ATF02) CASTLEFIELD
CORNELIOUS)
Horse/Passport: CASTLEFIELD CORNELIOUS/105KI20/USA
Person Responsible/ID/NF: Kaitlin CAMPBELL/10060519/USA
Event/Date: CSI5* MLSJ - Thermal CA (USA), 04-07.12.2024
Event Code: 2024_CI_0253_S_S_01
Date of sample collection: 07.12.2024
Prohibited Substance(s): Octopamine, Dexamethasone
Bar Code Nos.: 1489271
1

I. INTRODUCTION
1. This Decision pertains to the FEI case (2025/BS07(2025/ATF02) CASTLEFIELD CORNELIOUS)
(the “Horse”). In respect of this case, the FEI notified the PR that a violation of Article 2.1 (the
Presence of a Controlled Medication Substance and/or its Metabolites or Markers in a
Horse’s Sample) and Article 2.2 (the Use of a Controlled Medication Substance and/or
Controlled Medication Method) of the Equine Controlled Medication Rules (“ECMRs”) and
Article 2.1 (The Presence of a Banned Substance and/or its Metabolites or Markers in a
Horse’s Sample) and Article 2.2 (the Use of a Banned Substance and/or Banned Method) of
the Equine Anti-Doping Rules (the “EADRs”) had occurred based on the adverse analytical
findings (the “AAFs”) of Synephrine, Octopamine and Dexamethasone in the Horse’s sample.
2. The positive findings of Octopamine and Dexamethasone in the Horse’s sample gave rise to
an Anti-Doping Rule Violation under Article 2.1 and Article 2.2 of the EADCMRs collected at
the CSI5* MLSJ - Thermal CA (USA), 04-07.12.2024 (the “Event”).
3. A Settlement Agreement between the FEI and the PR was agreed by the Parties on 19
September 2025 (the “Settlement Agreement”). The Settlement Agreement and the Exhibits
thereto are hereby incorporated herein by reference.
II. Applicable Rule Provisions:
Statutes 25th edition, effective 21st November 2023 (the “Statutes”).
General Regulations 24th edition, 1 January 2020, updates effective 1 January 2024.
(the “GRs”) updates effective 1 January 2024 (the “GRs”).
FEI Equine Anti-Doping and Controlled Medication Regulations ("EADCMRs"), 3rd edition, 1
January 2021, updates effective 1 January 2023.
Internal Regulations of the FEI Tribunal, 3rd Edition, 1 February 2025 (“the IRs”).
III. PARTIES
4. Ms Kaitlin Campbell, (FEI ID 10060519), the PR in accordance with Article 118.3 of the GRs, is
an Athlete in the discipline of Jumping for the United States of America (the “USA”), who
competed with the Horse at the Event.
2

5. The FEI is the IOC-recognised international governing body for the equestrian sport
disciplines of Dressage and Para-Equestrian Dressage, Jumping, Eventing, Driving and Para-
Driving, Endurance and Vaulting.
IV. FACTUAL BACKGROUND
6. The Horse was tested during the Event and returned positive results for Synephrine,
Octopamine and Dexamethasone.
7. Synephrine is classified as an Atypical Finding (“ATF”) substance under the FEI Atypical Findings
Policy (the “ATF Policy”). As such, the PR was first invited to provide an explanation for the
Synephrine finding to be considered by the ATF Panel.
8. Octopamine is classified as a Banned Substance and Dexamethasone is classified as a
Controlled Medication Substance under the FEI Equine Prohibited Substances List (the “List”).
The PR was informed that the proceedings relating to these findings would be notified once the
ATF proceedings in relation to Synephrine had concluded.
9. On 11 March 2025, the PR provided an explanation to the ATF Panel regarding Synephrine. The
PR submitted that the source was teff hay. On 7 May 2025, the FEI notified the PR that the ATF
Panel had accepted that the PR had proven that the source of the Synephrine was teff hay and
had thus closed the case in relation to Synephrine with no consequences. By the same letter,
the FEI informed the PR that she would receive “further notification from the FEI in relation to
the finding of Octopamine and Dexamethasone”.
10. By Notification Letter dated 16 June 2025 (the “Notification Letter”), the FEI informed the PR of
a potential violation of Articles 2.1 and 2.2 of the EADCMRs based on the findings for
Octopamine and Dexamethasone in the Sample. The PR was also notified in said letter that she
was provisionally suspended under Article 7.4.1 of the EADRs, and the Horse was also
provisionally suspended for two months until 15 August 2025.
11. In the Notification Letter, the FEI also explained to the PR that in accordance with Article 10.8.2
of the EADCMRs, if “the Person Responsible and/or member of the Support Personnel and/or
other Person admits an ECM/EAD Rule violation after being confronted with the ECM/EAD Rule
violation by the FEI and agrees to Consequences acceptable to the FEI” they may enter into a
Case Resolution Agreement and agree to Consequences acceptable at the sole discretion of
the FEI. The agreement shall be submitted to the FEI Tribunal (the “Tribunal”) for the sole
3

purpose of the Tribunal confirming that the criteria set forth in the EADCMRs have been fulfilled
(or do not apply) and, where so confirmed by the Tribunal, the final agreement shall state the
full reasons for any period of Ineligibility agreed, including (if applicable), a justification for why
the flexibility in sanction was applied.
12. On 5 September 2025, the PR requested the urgent lifting of the provisional suspension in
accordance with Article 7.4.4 (ii) of the EADR. The FEI consented to that request.
13. On 8 September 2025, the FEI Tribunal lifted the provisional suspension with effect
from midnight CET.
14. On 19 September 2025, the FEI submitted the Settlement Agreement with Exhibits for the
approval of the Tribunal and requested for a Panel to be appointed for the purpose or review
and approval of the said Settlement Agreement.
15. On 27 October 2025, the Tribunal informed the Parties of the appointment of a one person
hearing panel to adjudicate and approve this case. The Parties were asked to provide any
objections to the constitution of the hearing panel. On 27 October 2025, both the PR and
the FEI confirmed having no objections to the constitution of the hearing panel.
V. ACCEPTED TERMS
16. The Settlement Agreement is made in accordance with Article 10.8.2 of the EADRs, Article
10.8.2 of the ECMRs and is subject to the approval of the Tribunal.
NOW, THEREFORE, THE PARTIES HAVE AGREED TO THE FOLLOWING
TERMS FOR THE CLOSURE OF THE PROCEEDINGS:
17. In the matter related to the Sample, which was collected from the PR’s horse CASTLEFIELD
CORNELIOUS at the CSI5* MLSJ - Thermal CA (USA), on 7 December 2024, the PR, Ms Kaitlin
Campbell, and the FEI agree in accordance with 10.8.2 of the EADR and Article 10.8.2 of the
ECMR on the following:
a) The PR admits the violation of Article 2.1 (Presence of a Banned Substance in a Horse’s
Sample) and Article 2.2 (Use of a Banned Substance) of the EADR and Article 2.1
(Presence of a Controlled Medication Substance in a Horse’s Sample) and Article 2.2 (Use
of a Controlled Medication Substance) of the ECMR;
4

b) Pursuant to Article 10.9.5 of the EADR and Article 10.9.4 of the ECMR, the PR will be
considered to have committed one rule violation in respect of the Octopamine and
Dexamethasone findings, and the sanction will be based on the Banned Substance
(Octopamine);
c) The PR has established, on the balance of probabilities, how Octopamine entered the
Horse’s system;
d) The PR has established that she bore No Fault or Negligence for the Octopamine rule
violation in accordance with Article 10.5 of the EADR;
e) Therefore, no period of Ineligibility shall be imposed on the PR;
f) The results achieved by the PR and the Horse at the Event are disqualified, with all
resulting consequences, including forfeiture of any related medals, points and prizes, in
accordance with Articles 9.1 and 10.1.2 of the EADR;
g) The PR shall not incur any fine;
h) No other sanctions will apply in this case;
i) Each party will bear its own legal and other costs incurred in connection with
these proceedings;
j) In accordance with Article 10.9.2 of the EADR and Article 10.9.2 of the ECMR, the Rule
Violation shall not be considered a prior violation for the purpose of Article 10.9 (Multiple
Violations) of the EADR or ECMR.
18. This agreement is made in accordance with Article 10.8.2 of the EADR and Article 10.8.2 of
the ECMR and is subject to the approval of the FEI Tribunal. The Parties hereby kindly request
that the FEI Tribunal issue a Decision incorporating the terms of this agreement.
19. In accordance with Article 10.8.2 of the EADR and Article 10.8.2 of the ECMR, the FEI’s
decision to enter or not enter into a case resolution agreement, and the amount of the
reduction to, and the starting date of, the otherwise applicable period of Ineligibility and the
confirmation of the case resolution agreement by the FEI Tribunal are not subject to appeal
under Article 13 of the EADR or Article 12 of the ECMR.
5

20. The Parties acknowledge and agree that pursuant to Article 14.3 of the EADR and Article 13.3
of the ECMR, the Decision will be made public by the FEI.
21. The terms set out in this agreement have been agreed as a full and final settlement of all
claims relating to the subject matter of these proceedings. Accordingly, any and all other
claims for relief that any Party might otherwise have made against another in relation to the
subject-matter of these proceedings are released and discharged unconditionally, and they
may not be pursued in any form hereafter.
VI. DECISION
22. The Tribunal has jurisdiction over this matter pursuant to Article 38 of the Statutes, Article
161 of the GRs, the EADCMRs, Article 18 of the IRs. The PR is a member of the USA-NF, which
is a member of the FEI. The PR is therefore bound by the EADRs and ECMRs.
23. Having reviewed the case summary, the full reasoning of the Settlement Agreement and the
Accepted Terms, the Hearing Panel accepts that the FEI found that the PR had established,
on a balance of probabilities, how Octopamine entered the Horse’s system.
24. The Tribunal further acknowledges that the PR and the FEI have agreed on the terms for the
closure of the proceedings, in accordance with Article 10.8.2 of the EADRs, as detailed under
Section V of this Decision.
25. The Tribunal confirms that the Accepted Terms of the Settlement Agreement comply with
the EADRs and ECMRs and finds no grounds to object thereto.
26. The Parties acknowledge and agree that pursuant to Article 14.3 of the EADRs and Article
13.3 of the ECMRs, this Final Decision will be made public by the FEI. The terms set out in the
Settlement Agreement are a full and final settlement of all claims relating to the subject
matter of these proceedings.
27. The Settlement Agreement and this Decision are not subject to appeal under Article 13 of
the EADRs or Article 12 of the ECMRs.
DECISION TO BE FORWARDED TO:
a. The Parties: Yes
6

b. The NF of the PR: Yes
c. Any other: No
